## Which file do I need?

| You want to… | Download |
|---|---|
| Play straight away on any computer | **cognitive-terrain-0.14.1.html**, then double-click it to open in your browser |
| Read the rules | **Cognitive-Terrain-Field-Manual-0.14.1.pdf** |
| Install it like a normal program | **…-Setup.exe** (Windows), **…-macOS-AppleSilicon.zip** or **…-macOS-Intel.zip** (Mac), **…-Linux.tar.gz** |
| Host it on itch.io | **…-web.zip** |

The installers are not code-signed yet, so Windows and macOS warn on first
launch. **PLAYTEST-README.txt** explains how to get past the warning.

Two-player games work between any of these files, as long as both players
use version 0.14.1.

## What's new

- **Music on the playtest page.** Night Watch, the game's main theme, plays on
  the page: it fades in on arrival, or at the first click where the browser
  holds sound back. A Music button turns it off, and the choice is remembered.
  The loop is recorded from the game's own soundtrack (`audio/night-watch.mp3`).
- **How the game was made.** The start screen, the field manual's credits,
  README and ATTRIBUTION.md now set out the designer's role (concept, design,
  rules, sources, opponents, campaigns and final review) and note that AI
  tools helped with code and drafting under his direction. No AI runs while
  you play.
- **Source check.** Every real-world claim in the game and the manual was
  checked against the cited research. Wording was tightened where it went
  further than a source (section references, two quotations, the AI Agents and
  AI Vulnerability Mapping years now marked as estimates, which innovation
  scores are the paper's and which are the designer's), and text that is a
  game assumption is now labelled as one. No statistic or quotation had to be
  removed.
- No rule changes. Two-player codes work between 0.14 builds.

> **Designer's note:** this one is purely for fun. A wargame becomes memorable when it is engaging.
> Night Watch was written to sound like the quiet hours on an
> operations floor. It seemed a shame to keep it locked behind the start
> screen.
